maria_ml: Quick update — cassiopeia11b v1-int4 bring-up hit OOMs in canary. Pattern: microbatch >= 8 or long generations (max_new_tokens=1024) trigger CUDA OOM after ~20m, memory fragmentation climbs.
chris_runtime: Which infra pool? GPU type + total VRAM?
maria_ml: pool=alpha-gpu, A100-80G. Log excerpt:
```
E tensorflow/serving: CUDA OOM when allocating tensor of size 1.2GiB
vram usage snapshot: 47.2GiB / 80.0GiB (peak 78.9GiB)
Trace: allocate_kv_cache -> allocate_attention_buffers -> forward
```
lee_infra: Hm. Peak looks high for int4 even with long seqs. Two quick knobs: drop default max_new_tokens to 256 for production, and cap microbatch at 4. Also set `batch_timeout_ms` lower (10-20ms) so we don't accumulate huge implicit batches of long sequences.
ajenkins: Onboarding tip: disable KV prefetch on coldstart for this model (`kv_prefetch=false`) — we've seen prefetch thrash cause slot fragmentation for similar architectures. Also enable `slot_compactor=true` and `slot_reserve=0.12` to reduce fragmentation mid-run.
maria_ml: Good call. Reproduced locally with `--max_new_tokens=1024 --microbatch=8` — frag spikes. With `max_new_tokens=256` + `microbatch=4` it's stable in 1h smoke.
nina_prod: If we lower max_new_tokens, any fallback plan for customers needing longer outputs? 6b variant ready?
maria_ml: We have cassiopeia-6b-lite but quality is ~5-7% lower on our eval set. Plan: canary rollout with cassiopeia11b v1-int4 + conservative defaults (max_new_tokens=256, microbatch_max=4, kv_prefetch=false, slot_reserve=0.12). If long-gen requested, route to 6b variant as a temporary fallback and surface quality delta in the response metadata.
devops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary cassiopeia11b v1-int4 -> pool alpha at 2026-03-24T07:00:00Z
chris_runtime: Please add an automated long-gen smoke test (>=512 tokens) to the canary gate and alert if OOMs >0.1% or frag metric >0.2.
maria_ml: Added eval set + perf dashboard. Alerting on OOM rate and slot fragmentation. Will post results after 12h canary run.
chris_runtime: Nice. Thanks — keep the perf notes in the model card and add the two conservative defaults to onboarding docs. :+1:
maria_ml: Will do. :thumbsup:
